signals.name: Attention spike (any)
signals.definition: Daily Wikipedia page views >= 3x the median of the prior 60 days and >= 1,000 views. No direction is assumed; tested two-sided.

signals.name: Spike after a rally
signals.definition: Attention spike following a >= 10% rise over the prior 5 trading days.
signals.rationale: Attention-grabbing winners attract uninformed buying that later reverses (Barber & Odean 2008).

signals.name: Spike after a sell-off
signals.definition: Attention spike following a >= 10% fall over the prior 5 trading days. No direction assumed.
signals.rationale: Separates news-driven attention on losers from attention on winners.

signals.name: Spike without a price move
signals.definition: Attention spike while the prior 5-day return is within ±5%.
signals.rationale: Attention not yet reflected in price — does price follow?

signals.name: Sustained attention build
signals.definition: 28-day average views >= 2x the prior 182-day average, with >= 500 views/day.
signals.rationale: Rising retail attention creates short-run buying pressure (Da, Engelberg & Gao 2011).

coverage.note: Pageviews are fetched from a throttled API; coverage below 100% is the unfetched tail of an arbitrary Wikidata ordering (equal by exchange). Companies below the view thresholds never trigger.
